messages:
cheng: Heads up — saw a bunch of orphan spans for jobs processed by our workers. Traces show worker spans with no parent. Looks like when the gateway publishes to SQS the trace headers are getting dropped. Anyone seen this before?

bryan: seen it once. quick repro: gateway -> SQS (MessageAttributes) -> worker (go) -> exporter. Worker spans end up as roots. logs: `Received msg id=abc123 no traceparent header`

maria: can you paste the raw message attributes the gateway is setting?

cheng: here is what gateway currently sets:
```
MessageAttributes: {
  "traceparent": { DataType: 'String', StringValue: '00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01' },
  "baggage": { DataType: 'String', StringValue: 'userId=123' }
}
```
worker-side shows header missing. my suspicion: our fanout envelope re-serializes attributes into a `headers` JSON string for compat and that step strips typed MessageAttributes, so they never make it to the final SQS record the worker reads.

bryan: note: some SDKs and middleware will coerce attribute keys to lowercase or change types (String vs Binary). our go consumer expects `traceparent` or `Traceparent`? which exact key do we check for?

cheng: worker code (go-otel helper) looks for `traceparent` and `tracestate` top-level in attributes. gateway uses `traceparent` lowercased, but the envelope serializes attributes into a single `headers` JSON string. the worker only looks at top-level MessageAttributes, so mismatch. also saw that we sometimes base64 baggage which can make the attr binary and some serializers drop binary attrs.

maria: can you paste raw CloudWatch SQS message JSON (the one the worker receives)? small snippet is fine.

cheng: pasted snippet in the channel (omitted here) — essentially `MessageAttributes` was empty and `body.headers` had the previous attrs as a JSON string. worker not reading `body.headers`.

lina: proposal: standardize on top-level `traceparent` + `tracestate` as MessageAttributes for all producers. encode any potentially-binary values (baggage) as base64 and use a well-known key `x-rd-baggage-b64`. keep `baggage` as optional. also add a short compatibility flag `x-rd-trace-handshake: 1` which signals consumers to look in `body.headers` for legacy messages.

cheng: pragmatic immediate fix: add fallback in worker to parse `body.headers` JSON and extract `traceparent` if top-level attributes missing. I'll open a PR for that today.

bryan: longer-term: gateway should stop embedding attrs into `body.headers` and instead set real MessageAttributes. add unit tests and an integration test that roundtrips headers through SQS. I'll open a gateway PR after cheng's worker patch.

maria: I'll add a dashboard tile for "orphan spans by queue" (span has no parent_id and non-empty service=worker). alert when rate > 0.5% over 5m. also add a small table listing most recent message ids for manual inspection.

cheng: timeline: worker fallback PR today, gateway attr-fix PR tomorrow, canary next week.

devops-bot: deployment requested by cheng — canary: msg-ctx-fallback -> staging

devops-bot: canary deployed (staging) :white_check_mark:

bryan: one more question about sampling: if header is missing, do we create a new root span or try to stitch using `queue.message_id`? I prefer starting a new root to avoid mis-attributing, but include the original trace id (if we can reconstruct) as an attribute like `queue.parent_trace_id` so post-processing can stitch.

lina: agree. new root is safer for production metrics. include `queue.message_id` and `queue.attributes.traceparent_fallback` fields so we have signals for reprocessing.

maria: I'll add a small reprocessing job to attempt to retroactively link orphan spans where logs and message artifacts allow. we'll surface stitched links in the dashboard for manual review.

cheng: gotcha: delayed retries and visibility timeout may create multiple roots for the same logical request. dashboard dedupe logic should consider `queue.message_id` + short time window.

bryan: PRs: https://github.com/redwood/gateway/pull/891 (adds traceparent top-level attr + tests) and https://github.com/redwood/worker/pull/132 (fallback extractor + unit tests).

maria: can we add a simple runbook checklist for verifying traces after canary? e.g. 1) publish test message with known traceparent -> 2) confirm worker span is child in APM -> 3) confirm orphan rate drops to 0 for test queue.

lina: I'll draft the runbook and ping ops.

cheng: thanks everyone — big improvement for telemetry quality :thumbsup:
